See also: горя, ropa, Appendix:Variations of "gora", and Appendix:Variations of "hora"

Belarusian

[edit]

Etymology

[edit]

Inherited from Proto-Slavic *goře. Related to гарэ́ць (harécʹ, “to burn, to be consumed by fire”). Cognates include Russian го́ре (góre), Ukrainian го́ре (hóre).

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • IPA(key): [ˈɣora]
This entry needs an audio pronunciation. If you are a native speaker with a microphone, please record this word. The recorded pronunciation will appear here when it's ready.

Noun

[edit]

го́ра • (hóra) n inan (genitive го́ра, uncountable)

  1. (uncountable) grief, distress, sadness
  2. (uncountable) trouble
  3. (uncountable) misfortune, disaster

Declension

[edit]
Declension of го́ра (inan sg-only hard neut-form accent-a)

locative го́ры
hóry

Bulgarian

[edit]
Bulgarian Wikipedia has an article on:
гора
Wikipedia bg

Etymology

[edit]

From Proto-Slavic *gora, from Proto-Balto-Slavic *garā́ˀ.

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • IPA(key): [ɡoˈra]
  • Audio (Standard Bulgarian):(file)
  • Rhymes: -ra
  • Syllabification(key): го‧ра

Noun

[edit]

гора́ • (gorá) f (relational adjective го́рски, diminutive гори́ца or гори́чка, augmentative гори́ще)

  1. wood, forest, woods
  2. (obsolete, used in names) mountain
    Synonym: планина́ (planiná)
    Сре́дна гора́ ― Srédna gorá ― Sredna Gora (literally, “Middle Mountain”)

Declension

[edit]
Declension of гора́

gorí
definite гора́та
goráta 		гори́те
goríte
vocative form го́ро
góro 		гори́
gorí

References

[edit]

  • “гора”, in Речник на българския език [Dictionary of the Bulgarian Language] (in Bulgarian), Chitanka, 2010

Anagrams

[edit]
  • агро- (agro-), арго (argo), рога (roga)

Macedonian

[edit]

Etymology

[edit]

Inherited from Proto-Slavic *gora, from Proto-Balto-Slavic *garā́ˀ.

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • IPA(key): [ˈɡɔɾa]
  • Audio:(file)
  • Hyphenation: го‧ра

Noun

[edit]

гора • (gora) f (plural гори, relational adjective горски, diminutive горичка or горица)

  1. forest
    Synonym: шума f (šuma)
  2. (archaic) mountain
    Synonym: планина f (planina)

Old Church Slavonic

[edit]

Etymology

[edit]

From Proto-Slavic *gora, from Proto-Balto-Slavic *garā́ˀ.

Noun

[edit]

гора • (gora) f

  1. mountain
    • from Vita Methodii, 0700300-0700310:
      а тꙑ любиши гороу вельми, то не мози горꙑ ради оставити оучениꙗ своѥго, паче бо можеши кꙑмь съпасенъ бꙑти.
      a ty ljubiši goru velĭmi, to ne mozi gory radi ostaviti učenija svojego, pače bo možeši kymĭ sŭpasenŭ byti.
      Though you have great love for the mountain, still leave not your teaching for the mountain’s sake, for you can sooner be saved through it.

Pannonian Rusyn

[edit]

Etymology

[edit]

Inherited from Old Slovak hora, from Proto-Slavic *gora. Cognates include Carpathian Rusyn гора́ (horá) and Slovak hora.

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • IPA(key): [ˈɦɔra]
  • Rhymes: -ɔra
  • Hyphenation: го‧ра

Noun

[edit]

гора (hora) f (relational adjective горски)

  1. mountain
    за седем горами ― za sedem horami ― very far (literally, “beyond seven mountains”)

Declension

[edit]
Declension of гора (hora)
singular plural
nominative гора (hora) гори (hori)
genitive гори (hori) горох (horox)
dative гори (hori) гором (horom)
accusative гору (horu) гори (hori)
instrumental гору (horu) горами (horami)
locative гори (hori) горох (horox)
vocative горо (horo) гори (hori)

Related terms

[edit]
adjectives
  • горнї (hornji)
adverbs
  • горе (hore)
nouns
  • горец m pers (horec)
  • горяк m pers (horjak)
  • загорє n (zahorje)
  • медзигорє n (medzihorje)
  • подгорє n (podhorje)
  • предгорє n (predhorje)
  • пригорє n (prihorje)
prepositions
  • горе (hore)
proper nouns
  • Горняк m pers (Hornjak)
  • Чарна Гора f (Čarna Hora)

[edit]
  • Medʹeši, H.; Fejsa, M.; Timko-Djitko, O. (2010), “гора”, in Ramač, Ju., editor, Руско-сербски словнїк [Rusyn-Serbian Dictionary] (in Pannonian Rusyn), Novi Sad: Faculty of Philosophy
  • Fejsa, M.; Šlemender, M.; Čelʹovski, S. (2022), “mountain”, in Анґлийско-руски словнїк [English-Rusyn Dictionary] (in Pannonian Rusyn), Novi Sad: Faculty of Philosophy; Ruska matka, →ISBN, page 184

Inherited from Proto-Slavic *gora, from Proto-Balto-Slavic *garā́ˀ.

  • Audio:(file)

[edit]

Serbo-Croatian

[edit]

Etymology

[edit]

Inherited from Proto-Slavic *gora, from Proto-Balto-Slavic *garā́ˀ.

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • IPA(key): /ɡǒra/
  • Hyphenation: го‧ра

Noun

[edit]

го̀ра f (Latin spelling gòra)

  1. mountain
  2. (regional, Croatia) hill, highland
  3. (by extension, Croatia) forest, woods (forested hilly area)

Ukrainian

 гора on Ukrainian Wikipedia

Etymology

[edit]

Inherited from Middle Ukrainian *гора f (*hora, “a mountain”), from Old East Slavic гора f (gora, “a mountain”), from Proto-Slavic *gorà f (“a mountain”), from Proto-Balto-Slavic *garā́ˀ f (“a forest”), from Proto-Indo-European *gʷorH-eh₂.

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • IPA(key): [ɦɔˈra]
  • Audio:(file)
  • Hyphenation: го‧ра́

Noun

[edit]

  1. mountain
